title: "Covered Interest Parity Deviations in Emerging Market Currencies"

::: {.status}
Still in progress.
:::

Covered interest parity says that borrowing in one currency, converting
it, and hedging the exchange rate with a forward should cost the same as
borrowing in the other currency directly. Before 2008 that held almost
exactly for the major currencies. Since then it hasn't, and the gap (the
cross-currency basis) has stayed open for years in a way textbook
arbitrage says it shouldn't.

The best-known work on this focuses on G10 pairs. This project looks at
emerging-market currencies instead, where capital controls, thinner
forward markets, and dollar funding pressure should all matter more.

The data, method, and results will go up here once they're solid enough
to show. Until then, this page is a placeholder for the project.
